title: Volunteering at the shelter
text:
Hi Emily,

How are you? I hope your exams went well! I wanted to tell you about something new in my life: since September I've been volunteering at an animal shelter on the edge of town.

I go there every Wednesday afternoon and on Saturday mornings. At first I thought I would just play with puppies, but the work is much harder than that! We clean the cages, prepare food, wash the dogs and take them for long walks in the forest. Some of the animals have been badly treated, so they are scared of people. It can take weeks before they let you touch them.

My favourite dog is called Bruno. He's an old, grey dog with only three legs – he lost one in an accident. When he arrived, he hid in the corner and didn't eat for two days. Now he runs to the gate as soon as he sees me! The staff say he probably won't find a new family because most people want young dogs. I'm trying to convince my parents to adopt him, but our flat is quite small and Dad isn't keen.

The best moment so far was when a family came to take home a cat that had lived at the shelter for over a year. Everybody cried, even the manager!

If you're interested, the shelter always needs volunteers. You don't need any experience – they give you training on the first day. And if you can't give your time, they're happy to receive old blankets and towels.

Write soon and tell me your news!
Hugs,
Martyna
